about: The checklist a world-edit compatibility evaluation must account for (Q42, roadmap 4.23). Domain knowledge only: which families exist, what each check is about, what it may claim and where it stops. The controller (_geometry-harness/evalrun.py) reads it through _geometry-harness/evalregistry.py and never decides applicability itself. Triggers name record-type families as DOMAIN knowledge; what a target actually contains comes from scopeprobe, by construction, out of Mutagen's own record enumeration. Check ids are stable: retired, never renamed.

notes.recordTypeKeys: anyType operands are the four-character record type signatures scopeprobe keys `recordTypes` by; the Mutagen registration class name travels beside each count as `className`.
notes.adapterArgs: adapter.args is the argv shape the check needs, with placeholders the controller fills: {order} {emit} {base} {json} {target} {switchMap} {pair} {nexusId} {out}. For kind ordersweep-probe the shape is what ordersweep.py hands the probe; the controller passes the exe name to `ordersweep.py --probes`, it does not spawn the probe itself.
notes.claimRows: evidence.claim names the row in _claude/GlobalDocs/CLAIMS.md a finding reports under. null means the ledger has no row for this check; evidence.limits then says why, and a finding from it is never upgraded to a ledger claim.
notes.unmeasuredExtents: scope.json's `unmeasured` is a list of {extent, why} over the closed vocabulary script-placement, alias-fill, bos-swaps, asset-replacers, door-destinations, generated-output (PLAN amendment A-1). A check may declare applicability.dependsOnExtents naming any of them; evalregistry then answers unknown whenever the scope lists one, whatever the trigger says.
notes.triggerFields: Each trigger key reads one scope field and nothing else: placed -> placed.total, exterior -> placed.exterior, land -> placed.land, navmesh -> placed.navm, anyType -> recordTypes, overlays -> configuration.overlays, nexusId -> nexusId, masters -> masters; always reads nothing. placedMeshes reads no scope field: it reads the mesh reach (scope/mesh-reach.json, written by overlapprobe --mesh-reach on the combined arm), credited -> yes, a complete reach with none credited -> no, none or an incomplete reach -> unknown.
notes.adapterResult: A-6: a check whose adapter output is json or text carries adapter.result {kind, findings, judged, unjudgeable}. A spec is a dotted path into the child's JSON output (a number is that number, a list is its length) or regex:<pattern> with a named group `n` over the child's log. A null spec means the probe prints no such count -- adapter.result.note says so, and the controller records the gap rather than reading a number that means something else. kind detector reads finding when findings > 0, else no-finding; catalogue and discovery read catalogue. scopeprobe is excepted (D2's `complete` field). A kind that runs no child (derived, manual, unsupported) has output null: there is no child output to read.
notes.commonFlags: A-10(b): --instance/--profile/--game are passed only where adapter.commonFlags is true. blockprobe parses no --instance at all (grepped) and finds the instance through HarnessTarget (the patch-discovery probes' rows left for the houseCARL integration module's list in step 3 of the boundary), which reads HOUSECARL_MO2_INSTANCE / HOUSECARL_MO2_PROFILE / HOUSECARL_GAME_PATH from the environment every child gets. A placeholder is substituted in the shape the args give it: a bare {target} is positional, --target {target} is a flag.
notes.population: A-10(d)/A-11(d): adapter.population / adapter.state name the population a probe's emit actually declares when it is not the arm's, so the receipt validator compares the emit against the probe's own words rather than the plan's. Three probes differ, each for the same reason -- their population is not placed references: driftprobe (placement history), seamprobe (LAND heightmaps) and waterprobe (CELL water records). navownprobe, overlapprobe, contactprobe and stateprobe emit load-time/baseline and declare nothing.

checks.title: The target's masters resolve and the evaluated order is one the engine would load

applicability.note: Every arm is an order, and an order the engine would refuse has no findings worth reading. scopeprobe resolves the configuration through HarnessOrderCli, which refuses a plugin ahead of its master, an absent master or a non-master ahead of a master-flagged plugin; on an arm that refusal IS this check's finding.

evidence.limits: The claim ledger has no row for loadability: it is a record fact read off the plugin headers and the resolver's own refusal rules, not a detector class with a floor and a control. It says the order loads and what it contains; it says nothing about whether the content is compatible.

checks.title: Navmesh edits discarded by a later plugin, and the integrity of the winning mesh's links

applicability.note: A target that cuts navmesh can discard another plugin's cut; a target that only places references can still be the later plugin whose re-cut discards one, and its own placements are the UNCUT census's population. Either footprint needs the check.

evidence.claim: CLOBBERED (with DANGLE / EDGE-IDX and UNCUT); DOOR-IDX is retired and off unless --door-idx is passed
evidence.limits: CLOBBERED reports a LOST EDIT, never broken pathing; a row Holds on the 120 u victim-only-ground predicate and becomes a finding only with a witness. Connectivity is the selector's stated blind spot both ways. UNCUT is a census, not a verdict. Class A (Bethesda-on-Bethesda) is withheld.

checks.title: References placed or moved into another plugin's reference

applicability.note: The population is placed references and the meshes they use. A target that files something under a cell can introduce an intersection; so can a selected mod folder whose mesh wins for a placed reference and differs from the one it replaces, with a plugin or without one. Not applicable only when both are measured false.

evidence.limits: Actual placed strict NIF render surfaces decide crossing, coplanar overlap, touching and separation; validated closed-solid containment is separate evidence. Bounds only accelerate safe rejection, with no box depth, fraction or size decision gate. The population is the LOAD-TIME enable state, not the reference flag alone. Introduced-vs-Inherited requires a measured counterfactual; missing geometry or unfinished work remains unknown. Geometric intersection does not establish harmful or unintended overlap. Historical bounds policies are not comparable for repair credit.

checks.title: Dependents left touching nothing after a later plugin moved their host

applicability.note: The population is placed references and the surfaces they rest on. A target that files something under a cell can break a contact; so can a selected mod folder whose mesh wins for a placed reference and differs from the one it replaces (a reshaped host or dependent), with a plugin or without one. Not applicable only when both are measured false.

evidence.limits: Fixed dependents only, judged within epsilon against the arm's own load-time enable state per arm. A dependent that was never touching as authored is out of the population.

checks.title: Fixtures left hanging in empty space after another mod removed the room around them

applicability.note: The population is placed fixtures and the floors and walls they stand on or against; nothing filed under a cell means no room to remove.

evidence.limits: Interiors only (the land is not read). A fixture is left in empty space when everything it touches, followed from piece to piece (and the items its weapon racks mount), reached a floor or wall that a later plugin removed or moved, and reaches none under the winner. A floor or wall is a Static with solid collision at least 64 u across that the fixture's own plugin does not define (a Bethesda master's always count); that gate is a stated parameter, not measured in game. The weapon-rack case was seen in game (the 2026-10-13 lab block: racks and swords hanging in the void another mod's disable left); no row of this check has been confirmed in game by itself. Loose items that are not held fall instead and are the rest rule's business. Fixtures that exist only after a quest flips their switch are judged by state.conditional-geometry's empty-space pass. The Bethesda floor is withheld.

checks.title: Placed references left floating or buried after another mod reshaped the terrain under them

applicability.note: A clash needs a LAND edit on one side and an exterior reference on the other; either in the target is enough to have to look.

evidence.limits: Built (contactprobe --terrain) and measured, not yet admitted. The Bethesda-on-Bethesda burial floor passes the run plan's 2 % line at 32 u only at the registered surface share (0.25), which was chosen after inspecting the floor; at share 0.10 it fails. In game, the stations confirmed that a Fixed static keeps its position and that the ground follows the winning heightmap, and showed real-pair rows buried, but the positive-control stations did not settle a probe item in the arm with the control terrain.

checks.unsupportedReason: terrain support is built and measured but not admitted: its burial floor passes only at a share chosen after inspecting it, and the in-game positive controls did not confirm.

checks.title: Declared host edges (XESP / XLKR / XAPR) over the movement census

applicability.note: Declared edges exist only between placed references.

evidence.limits: A measured null, catalogue status: the declared slice of the movement census has produced no finding class. Optional, and a null result here says nothing about undeclared dependencies, which geometry.placement-contact measures physically.

checks.title: Base Object Swapper layer: which bases the game actually loads for the target's references

applicability.note: The configuration identity lists the *_SWAP.ini overlays it read. With no overlay there is no swap layer to account for; with one, every geometry answer is computed over swapped bases and the swap set is part of what a receipt consumed.

result.note: bosprobe's --json carries profile, plugins, inis and rows and no unjudgeable count; the lines the reader could not read as written are printed by --anomalies and are not in the file, so the spec is null rather than a number read off something else.

evidence.limits: No ledger row of its own: bosprobe is the reader the geometry probes apply, not a detector class. What it reports is which base each reference resolves to and which ini lines it could not read as written; those anomalies are the finding. Runtime BOS behaviour beyond the ini semantics is unmeasured.

checks.title: Placed objects standing across a corridor's path line

applicability.note: The population is the target's own placed obstacles against the corridors of the cells it stands in.

result.judged: regex:rule comparison, all on the same (?P<n>[\d,]+) references
result.unjudgeable: regex:navmesh triangles that could not be judged \(inset consumed them\): (?P<n>[\d,]+)
result.note: blockprobe prints its route-cut verdicts as a per-reference listing with no total line, so findings has no spec to read and the check reaches no verdict. Its --rows file (adapter.files) carries every listed row; the report shows the Blocked and LikelyBlocked objects in it as leads for an in-game check, never as findings.

evidence.limits: blockprobe reads each arm's candidate (--order) and is told the plan targets that arm loads, judged as one set; each listed reference names the target(s) that place it ({by ...}) and the output tallies the route-cut verdicts per target. An arm that loads no target is not-applicable. Q30's fold applies: a single object's clearance, not collective blockage.

checks.title: Quest aliases authored together that the winning order pulls apart

applicability.note: Aliases, scenes and packages are the wiring a split breaks, and an ACHR/REFR move is how it gets broken. Naming these kinds is domain knowledge; whether the target has any is scopeprobe's measurement.

evidence.limits: driftprobe has no --base, so there is no reverse arm and no physical differential credit for this class: a candidate's rows are compared as rows, and a repaired SPLIT cannot be credited the way conflictdiff credits a physical predicate. Aliases together at authoring means <= 600 u and the same cell; both actors' governing packages must be editor-anchored.

checks.title: What the target reaches outside its own cells: door destinations, neighbouring cells, outbound links

applicability.note: Cell overlap alone cannot exclude cross-cell, asset or linked dependencies (packet outcome 1). Anything filed under a cell can reach outside it, so the expansion must be accounted for. It declares dependsOnExtents on the four extents scopeprobe always states as unmeasured, so its applicability is UNKNOWN on every scope today -- the visible "unknown dependency extent" the packet asks for, rather than a quiet yes over an extent nothing measured.

evidence.limits: Derived from scope.expansion: the four-neighbour exterior cells, the resolved door destinations with their unresolved count, and the outbound form links by master. It is an EXTENT, not a verdict — it says where the evaluation would have to look, and the unresolved destinations plus the stated unmeasured extents are exactly what it cannot close.

checks.title: Whether the surviving navigable surface still connects the places actors must reach

applicability.note: Any navmesh edit or placed obstacle can take part in a collective blockage; no footprint short of an empty one rules it out.

evidence.claim: CLOBBERED (its stated blind spot) and ROUTE CUT (Q30's fold)
evidence.limits: Open research limit, not an adapter gap. Both existing route classes judge one object or one lost edit at a time: CLOBBERED names connectivity as its selector's blind spot in both directions, and ROUTE CUT was folded to a single object's clearance. Nothing measures whether several individually-passable changes jointly cut a route. Required, and therefore keeps every evaluation of a geometry target incomplete — which is the honest state.

checks.unsupportedReason: no detector measures collective route connectivity; it is an open limit in the claim ledger and this packet does not reopen detector research.

checks.title: The enable markers, their member sets and their triggers in the target's cells

applicability.note: A switch is an enable-parent relationship between placed references; the census is over the cells the target files things in.

evidence.limits: A census of switches and the triggers bound to them, not a verdict. Its --json output is the --switch-map the state arms consume, and it runs on EVERY arm (about 14 s each on the lab) because a candidate that reorders the plugins can change which switch wins: reusing the baseline's map would judge one arm's states with another arm's census, and running it only on the baseline leaves every candidate's state check blocked for want of a map. A switch whose binding the reader could not read as written is counted as an anomaly, never as absent.

checks.title: Geometry rows that appear only once an enable marker is flipped

applicability.note: A state-conditional row is a geometry row under a flipped switch; the population is the same placed references, resolved with those switches inverted.

evidence.limits: A Standard plan evaluates only the states it selected (none beyond the load-time state by default); a Deep plan evaluates every state stategen.py generates from each arm's own census (every switch alone and every quest stage's joint flip, handed over as --states-file), and lists what the generator could not express (a looping or unresolved chain, an ambiguous stage member, disabled singletons, player-parented references, unreadable plugins, and combinations beyond one stage) under `unassessed`. STATE-OVERLAP is explicitly unmeasured and withheld until strict placed render triangles are available in this evaluator; diagnostic boxes cannot establish overlap findings. State contact and route roles remain available under their separate geometry contracts. The changed measurement identity refuses comparison against legacy box-based state emits. Each state also reads LEFT IN EMPTY SPACE for the fixtures it brings in (--empty-space; STATE-EMPTY rows; interiors only), so a fixture that exists only after its quest flips a switch is judged where it appears. stateprobe has no --base, so there is no reverse arm and no physical differential credit for a state row. The Bethesda floor is withheld. Collision-marker primitives are decided only when the plan found station Q's measured table (evalrun plan --primitive-solidity, HOUSECARL_PRIMITIVE_SOLIDITY or primitiveSolidity in the harness config): one measured solid is a route obstacle by its invisible box (NPC pathing through it is inferred from the player measurement); without the table they stay unjudged and the plan and emit say so. Placed actors a state changes are never rows: one that leaves is set aside, one arriving over the navmesh, on the floor and clear of solids is judged from placement (not checked in game), and the rest are unjudged by cause.

checks.title: A winning CELL override whose water tuple disagrees with its neighbour at the boundary

applicability.note: The class is about CELL water statements and the seams they make with adjacent cells; either an exterior footprint or a CELL record in the target can produce one.

adapter.population: n/a (CELL water records; no placed-reference population)

evidence.limits: A difference from the last Bethesda/USSEP statement joined to a visible boundary; catalogue status in the ledger. No in-game observation of the water surface is implied.

checks.title: Edge-adjacent cells whose winning heightmaps disagree on a shared vertex

applicability.note: A seam needs a LAND edit, or an exterior footprint whose neighbour carries one. Either is enough to have to look.

evidence.limits: A vertex disagreement beyond epsilon, split Introduced Blind / Seen / Inherited; catalogue status in the ledger. A seam is a step or a gap in the heightmap, not an observed visual defect.

checks.title: Occlusion planes and room/portal evidence at supported scope

applicability.note: Occlusion planes are placed references (base 000017 PlaneMarker); a target that places nothing cannot move one.

evidence.limits: Part D is ACCEPTED at its bounded scope with a constructed positive; no qualifying natural positive was established in the sampled views, and there is no natural-defect detector to run. Optional, because requiring a check nothing can perform would make every evaluation incomplete for a reason no run can resolve. The gap is recorded in `unassessed`, not hidden.

checks.unsupportedReason: the Part D result is bounded to its constructed positive; no natural-defect occlusion detector exists to adapt.

checks.title: Lights and light fixtures one mod leaves broken for another

applicability.note: Lights, the fixtures they sit at and the walls they shine on are placed references; a target that places nothing cannot strand, hide or double a light.

result.unit: lighting subjects (a light, a fixture or a lit shape, once per class)
result.note: findings counts every listed row of every class, admitted or held (the app shows a held class's rows as held, from classes below); the over-limit count is summary.cannotTell and is never a finding.

evidence.limits: Read from the load order alone over four arrangements (the dependencies, the selection over them, the rest over them, the combination); a row is listed only when the combination reads positive and no single arrangement does. Base Object Swapper is not applied: a scene in which a _SWAP.ini names a member is not judged. Whether a stranded, hidden or doubled light looks wrong in game is not established (Gate D designs that test). The over-limit reading is a count and never a clash. Load-time state only; interiors and exteriors (a centre cell with its eight neighbours). A radius over 16,384 units, or over 4,096 units outdoors, is not judged.

classes.title: A light left with no fixture
classes.evidence: Provisional (Gate A review decision 5): 0 rows on Bethesda's sides of 62 hosted lights (95 % bound 4.7 %); 45 rows on Group 6, every one a light the patch author edited (C:/hc-runs/2026-11-26-lighting-check/GATE-A.md section 6; gate-b/null.txt; gate-b/compare-g6-rows.txt).

classes.title: A fixture left with no light
classes.held: no row of this class has been read against a real case yet (none on the development data)
classes.evidence: 0 of 62 lit fixtures on the Bethesda null (bound 4.7 %); Group 6 lists none (C:/hc-runs/2026-11-26-lighting-check/GATE-A.md section 6).

classes.title: A light behind a wall
classes.evidence: Provisional (decision 5): 0 of 158 enabled lights on the Bethesda null (bound 1.9 %); Group 6 lists 2, both shadow spotlights, flagged in the row (C:/hc-runs/2026-11-26-lighting-check/GATE-A.md section 6).

classes.title: A light that lights nothing
classes.evidence: Provisional (decisions 3 and 5): 0 of 158 on the Bethesda null; 39 rows on Group 6; worded as cleanup, safe to disable (C:/hc-runs/2026-11-26-lighting-check/GATE-A.md section 6).

classes.title: A fixture lit twice
classes.held: no row of this class has been read against a real case yet (none on the development data), and whether doubling shows in game is not measured
classes.evidence: 0 of 441 emitting fixtures on the Bethesda null (bound 0.7 %); no development row (C:/hc-runs/2026-11-26-lighting-check/GATE-A.md section 6).

classes.title: Over the light limit
classes.held: a count, never a clash: whether the game drops a light here is not yet known
classes.evidence: Shipped exteriors already exceed the reading; 0 of 6,854 shapes listed on Bethesda (C:/hc-runs/2026-11-26-lighting-check/GATE-A.md section 6).

checks.title: Generated output that must be rebuilt after this change: Occlusion.esp, DynDOLOD, xLODGen, Synthesis, Reqtificator

applicability.note: Generated output is derived from placed geometry; a target that places or moves references invalidates whatever was generated from the old placement. Whether a given tool's output is installed is a fact about the profile, which is why this is a stated need rather than a measurement.

evidence.limits: No detector. The regeneration need is a consequence of the change, not a finding about it, and re-running the generators is out of this packet's scope. A decision here records WHICH generated outputs the reviewer judged stale and why; it never asserts that they were regenerated.

checks.unsupportedReason: regenerating LOD, occlusion and patcher output is outside the controller's scope; the check exists so the need is recorded rather than forgotten.

checks.title: Which of the examined orders passes the checks that were actually run

applicability.note: Every evaluation has at least a baseline arm, so there is always an order evaluation to report — even when it reports one arm and no alternative.

evidence.limits: Derived from the ordersweep receipts: the per-candidate classification is retained VERBATIM and scoped to the probes that ran, and is never promoted into a whole-evaluation pass. REPAIRED only when a physical predicate goes Holds -> Gone; a row that changed hands is RECLASSIFIED, with no repair credit. Per-probe repaired / reclassified / created / unmeasured counts are kept apart: no sum across probes, no net, and a regression on any probe stays a regression.

checks.title: Which discovered candidates were actually evaluated, and which remain leads

applicability.note: The distinction between an evaluated payload and a lead has to be stated for every evaluation, including one that discovered nothing.

evidence.limits: A candidate is `qualified` only when the hash of an actual plugin file appears in an evaluated arm. A Nexus hit, a pool file or a FOMOD option is `unqualified` however well it matches by name. An ESP-only arm qualifies the plugin and not the mod: its meshes, scripts and installer choices were not staged.

checks.title: Crashes, stutter, appearance and gameplay under the evaluated configuration

applicability.note: Any configuration can crash or look wrong; no static footprint bounds it.

evidence.limits: NEVER inferable from static checks. No number of clean record and geometry checks establishes that the configuration does not crash, stutter or render wrongly; only a run of the game does, and this packet launches none. Optional so that its permanent absence does not swamp the completion signal, and always listed under `unassessed` so the report cannot imply it was covered.

checks.unsupportedReason: runtime behaviour requires running the game; the controller performs no launch and cannot infer it from static evidence.
